Directions - A sentence is given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Active/Passive voice.

Indian Space Research Organisation can achieve new milestones through its commercial arm.

options.text: New Milestones can achieved by Indian Space Research Organisation through its commercial arm.
New Milestones can be achieved by Indian Space Research Organisation through its commercial arm.
New Milestones can be achieve by Indian Space Research Organisation through its commercial arm.
New Milestones might be achieved by Indian Space Research Organisation through its commercial arm.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **New Milestones can be achieved by Indian Space Research Organisation through its commercial arm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The above-given sentence is in the **active voice**.
 
• We need to change it into **passive voice**.
 
• The following **steps** need to be taken for converting the sentence into passive voice:-
 
 
• The subject '**Indian Space Research Organisation**' of the active voice will become the object of the passive voice.
 
• The object 'new milestones' of the passive voice will become the subject of the active voice.
 
• Since modal verb has been used in the active voice, therefore, the passive voice will follow the given structure:-
 
• Active Voice - **Subject + modal verb*(can) *+ V₁ + Object.**
 
• Passive Voice - **Object + modal verb*(can)* + be + V₃ + Subject.**
 
 

**Therefore, the correct passive voice is** *New Milestones can be achieved by Indian Space Research Organisation through its commercial arm.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• When we convert active voice to passive voice, three things need to be kept in mind:-

 
 
• Change object into subject.
 
• Change subject into object.
 
• Always use the third form of the verb in the passive voice.
 
• Use 'by' before the new object.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• ऊपर दिया गया वाक्य **active voice**** **में है । 
 
• हमें इसे passive voice में बदलने की जरूरत है।
 
• वाक्य को passive voice में बदलने के लिए निम्नलिखित कदम उठाने की आवश्यकता है: -
 
 
• Active voice का विषय 'Indian Space Research Organisation' passive voice का उद्देश्य बन जाएगा।
 
• Active voice का ऑब्जेक्ट 'new milestones' passive voice का विषय बन जाएगा।
 
• चूंकि, Active voice में modal verb का उपयोग किया गया है, इसलिए, passive voice दी गई संरचना का अनुसरण करेगी: -
 
• Active Voice - Subject + modal verb*(can) *+ V1 + Object.
 
• Passive Voice - Object + modal verb*(can)* + be + V3 + Subject.

 ​
 
 

इसलिए, सही निष्क्रिय आवाज़ है *New Milestones can be achieved by Indian Space Research Organisation through its commercial arm.*

questions.question: In an exam, a student scored 40% on the first paper out of a total of 200. How much percentage should the student score in the second paper out of 200 if he has to get 60% marks overall?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since both papers carry equal maximum marks (200 each), the overall percentage is simply the average of the individual percentages.

Overall % = (Paper 1 % + Paper 2 %) ÷ 2

60% = (40% + Paper 2 %) ÷ 2

120% = 40% + Paper 2 % ⇒ Paper 2 % = 80%

**∴ The correct answer is 80%.**

**Given:**

Maximum marks for Paper 1 = 200

Maximum marks for Paper 2 = 200

Overall target percentage required = 60%

⇒ Marks obtained in Paper 1 = (40 ÷ 100) × 200 = 80 marks

⇒ Total maximum marks for both papers = 200 + 200 = 400

⇒ Target marks required overall = (60 ÷ 100) × 400 = 240 marks

⇒ Marks required in Paper 2 = Target marks required − Marks in Paper 1

⇒ Marks required in Paper 2 = 240 − 80 = 160 marks

⇒ Percentage required in Paper 2 = (160 ÷ 200) × 100

⇒ Percentage required = 80%

**∴ The correct answer is 80%.**

Average Percentage (Equal Base)

When calculating overall percentages for components with equal total bases, the combined percentage is strictly the simple average: Combined % = (P₁ + P₂) ÷ 2.

Weighted Average (Unequal Base)

If the total marks are unequal (say W₁ and W₂), the weighted average method is required: Overall % = (W₁P₁ + W₂P₂) ÷ (W₁ + W₂).

Percentage to Absolute Value

To convert any percentage to absolute marks, use the standard formula: Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Total Base.

**Given:**

Price of sugar surges (increases) by 25%.

Overall expenditure of the consumer remains constant.

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

Percentage Decrease = (Decrease in Value ÷ Original Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/15c48d79be2a3f78f06444fd94210a136083b0a003a8b76def5eed5371d24671.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the original price of sugar be ₹100 per kg and the original consumption be 100 kg.

⇒ Original Expenditure = Price × Consumption = 100 × 100 = ₹10,000

⇒ New Price = 100 + 25% of 100 = ₹125 per kg.

⇒ Since the expenditure remains constant, New Expenditure = ₹10,000

⇒ New Consumption = New Expenditure ÷ New Price = 10000 ÷ 125 = 80 kg.

⇒ Fall in consumption = Original Consumption − New Consumption = 100 − 80 = 20 kg.

⇒ Percentage fall in consumption = (20 ÷ 100) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Expenditure Concept

If Total Expenditure is constant, Price and Consumption are inversely proportional to each other, mathematically written as P₁ × C₁ = P₂ × C₂.

Price Reduction Rule

questions.question: Which of the following correctly explains the origin of Indian classical music?

options.text: Folk scales evolved into Jatis in the modern period.
Tala system gave rise to Ragas during the Vedic period.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ragas developed from ancient Jatis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian classical music has its roots in the **ancient Jatis**, which were melodic structures used in early Indian music traditions.
 
• **Jatis** served as the foundation for the evolution of **Ragas**, which are complex melodic frameworks used in classical music to evoke specific emotions and moods.
 
• The concept of Jatis can be traced back to the **Vedic period**, where the **Sama Veda** laid the groundwork for Indian music through chants and hymns. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• The **Raga system** developed over time, incorporating the ancient principles of Jatis and expanding them into intricate melodic patterns that form the basis of modern classical music.
 
• The **Tala system**, which governs rhythm in Indian classical music, evolved independently alongside Ragas, but did not directly give rise to them during the Vedic period. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• The claim that Jatis originated from medieval Ragas is inaccurate, as Jatis predate Ragas and were the precursor to their development. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• The statement suggesting folk scales evolved into Jatis in the modern period is also incorrect, as Jatis have an ancient origin linked to classical traditions, not folk music. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin of Indian Classical Music:**

 
 
• Indian classical music originated from the **Sama Veda**, which contained hymns and chants that were sung in specific melodic structures.
 
• **Jatis** were the initial melodic structures that served as the basis for the development of **Ragas**.
 
• Over time, these Jatis evolved into highly complex systems of melody known as **Ragas**, which are used in both Hindustani and Carnatic music traditions.
 
 
 
• **Features of Ragas:**
 
 
• **Ragas** are designed to evoke specific emotions, moods, or times of the day, and are central to Indian classical music performances.
 
• Each Raga has its own set of rules regarding the ascending and descending notes (**Arohana** and **Avarohana**), as well as specific notes and phrases that define its character.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of the Tala System:**
 
 
• The **Tala system**, which governs rhythm, evolved separately but complements the melodic aspect of Ragas in performances.
 
• **Talas** are rhythmic cycles consisting of beats, and their interaction with Ragas adds depth to musical compositions.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Jatis and Folk Scales:**
 
 
• **Jatis** are classical melodic structures rooted in ancient traditions, while **folk scales** are simpler and often tied to specific cultural or regional practices.
 
• Folk music played a role in influencing classical music, but Jatis were primarily derived from Vedic traditions rather than folk scales.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of Jatis:**

 
 
• **Jatis** were early melodic patterns that laid the foundation for Ragas, forming the backbone of Indian classical music.
 
• They were structured and codified in ancient texts like the **Natyashastra** by **Bharata**, which is considered a seminal work in Indian performing arts.
 
 
 
• **Development of Ragas:**
 
 
• Ragas evolved from the principles of Jatis and became highly sophisticated over centuries, influenced by regional, cultural, and philosophical ideas.
 
• They became prominent during the medieval period, with the advent of Hindustani and Carnatic classical traditions.

• Athletes generally use their **dominant leg** for take-off as it provides better strength, balance, and coordination.

• **Hang technique:** The athlete keeps the body elongated during flight to optimize aerodynamics and minimize backward rotation.
 
• **Landing technique:** Athletes aim to land forward by tucking their legs and arms to maximize the measured distance.
 
 
 
• **Important Considerations:**
 
 
• **Speed:** Achieving the highest possible speed during the run-up is essential for generating momentum.
 
• **Strength:** The dominant leg's strength plays a critical role in determining the take-off force.
 
• **Angle:** The take-off angle impacts the jump's height and distance. An angle of approximately **20 degrees** is considered ideal.
 
• **Coordination:** Proper synchronization of body movements ensures balance and efficiency during all phases of the jump.

__
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** was the first significant legislative attempt by the British government to regulate the affairs of the **East India Company** in India.
 
• It introduced reforms in the **Company’s administration** by changing its constitution in Britain and addressing the governance of territories in India.
 
• The Act sought to centralize administration and ensure better control over the **Company’s operations**, both in India and in Britain. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• It established a **Governor-General of Bengal** and a council to supervise and control the Company’s territorial acquisitions and administration in India.
 
• The Act also required the Company to submit its accounts and finances to the British government to ensure greater accountability. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• It did not primarily deal with the **Company’s military or trade control**, nor did it focus on foreign relations or shipping trade. These aspects were secondary or indirect outcomes of the administrative restructuring.
 
• The Act laid the foundation for subsequent laws and policies aimed at regulating the affairs of the East India Company. *Hence, the correct answer is Company’s constitution in Britain and territorial rule in India.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Provisions of the Regulating Act of 1773:**

 
 
• The Act provided for the appointment of a **Governor-General of Bengal**, assisted by a council of four members. The first Governor-General was **Warren Hastings**.
 
• It mandated that the **Company’s territories** in Bengal, Bombay, and Madras be overseen by the Governor-General of Bengal, establishing a central authority.
 
• The Act made the East India Company accountable to the **British Parliament**, requiring them to submit regular reports and accounts.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Regulating Act:**
 
 
• It marked the beginning of **British parliamentary control** over the East India Company’s operations in India.
 
• The Act attempted to address the widespread corruption and inefficiency in the administration of the Company’s territories.
 
• It laid the foundation for the establishment of a systematic and centralized administrative framework in India, influencing future reforms like the **Pitt’s India Act of 1784**.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of the Act:**
 
 
• The Act did not address the Company’s trade operations or military control directly.
 
• It faced criticism for its inability to fully curb corruption and inefficiencies within the Company’s administration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Aspects of the Regulating Act:**

 
 
• The Act established a **Supreme Court** in Calcutta in 1774 to administer justice in the Company’s territories.
 
• It marked the beginning of a dual system of government, where the Company retained commercial privileges, but administrative control shifted to the British Crown.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The Regulating Act was a precursor to future legislative measures such as the **Pitt’s India Act of 1784**, which further strengthened British control over the Company.
 
• It represented a shift in the nature of British involvement in India, transitioning from commercial exploitation to direct territorial governance.

questions.question: Which type of landslide involves rotational movement of material along a curved surface?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Slump**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **slump** is a type of landslide that occurs when a mass of earth or rock moves downhill along a curved surface, which is usually concave in shape.
 
• In a slump, the material moves as a coherent block or mass, maintaining its internal structure to a certain extent.
 
• This movement typically occurs due to a combination of gravitational forces and the loss of cohesive strength in the material, often triggered by factors such as water saturation, erosion, or human activities.
 
• The curved surface of the rupture is a defining characteristic of a slump, distinguishing it from other types of landslides such as rockslides or rockfalls.
 
• Slumps are more common in loose or unconsolidated soils and sediments, particularly in areas with steep slopes and weak base layers.
 
• The movement of material in a slump is rotational, meaning the top of the displaced material tilts backward while the bottom moves outward and downward.
 
• The presence of water often plays a crucial role in triggering slumps. Water reduces the friction between soil particles, making the slope less stable.
 
• Slumps are often seen in coastal cliffs, riverbanks, and areas with loose, unconsolidated materials, especially after heavy rainfall or during rapid erosion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Different Types of Landslides:**

 
 
• **Rockslide:** This involves a rapid downslope movement of large blocks of detached bedrock. It usually occurs on steep slopes and is typically triggered by earthquakes, weathering, or human activities.
 
• **Rockfall:** A sudden and fast movement of rocks or boulders from a steep slope or cliff. It is often caused by weathering, freeze-thaw cycles, or erosion.
 
• **Slump:** As discussed, this is a rotational movement of soil or rock along a concave surface, often influenced by water saturation or erosion.
 
• **Debris fall:** This involves a sudden fall of loose debris, such as soil, rocks, and vegetation, from a steep slope. It is similar to a rockfall but includes a mix of materials.
 
 
 
• **Common Causes of Landslides:**
 
 
• Heavy rainfall leading to saturation of soil and reduced cohesion.
 
• Earthquakes that disturb the stability of slopes.
 
• Human activities such as deforestation, mining, and construction.
 
• Volcanic eruptions that destabilize surrounding areas.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• The Thistle landslide in **Utah, United States** (1983) was one of the largest slumps in U.S. history, caused by heavy rainfall and snowmelt.
 
• Slumps are common in the coastal cliffs of California, where erosion and wave action contribute to slope instability.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Factors Influencing Slumps:**

 
 
• Slopes with clay or loose soil are more prone to slumps due to their weaker cohesive strength.
 
• Prolonged rainfall or water seepage can exacerbate the likelihood of slumps by reducing soil stability.
 
• Human activities such as improper land use, deforestation, or construction can increase the risk of slumping by destabilizing slopes.
 
 
 
• **Prevention Measures:**
 
 
• Planting vegetation to increase slope stability and reduce erosion.
 
• Constructing retaining walls to support slopes and prevent slippage.
 
• Implementing effective drainage systems to reduce water infiltration into the soil.

questions.question: Population density is the measure of —
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**People per square kilometre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Population density** is defined as the number of people living per unit of area, usually expressed as **people per square kilometre**. It is a key demographic measure used globally to understand human distribution in a given region.
 
• This metric helps in analyzing the population concentration in a particular geographical area, indicating whether the area is densely or sparsely populated. *Hence, the correct option is "People per square kilometre".*
 
• Other options such as "People per house," "People per village," or "People per family" are incorrect as they measure different aspects of population distribution or household composition rather than density. *Hence, these options are not relevant for population density.*
 
• **Population density** varies significantly across countries and regions due to factors like geography, climate, urbanization, and economic activities. For example, urban areas tend to have higher population density compared to rural regions.
 
• Population density is an important indicator for urban planning, resource allocation, and understanding social dynamics in a region. It provides insights into the pressure on land and resources. *Hence, understanding this metric is crucial.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of Population Density:**

 
 
• **Population density** helps policymakers and governments to plan infrastructure development, transportation, housing, and public services.
 
• Regions with **high population density** often face challenges like congestion, environmental degradation, and resource scarcity, while areas with **low density** might struggle with connectivity and access to services.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing Population Density:**
 
 
• **Geographical factors:** Areas with favorable climatic conditions, fertile land, and water availability tend to have higher population density.
 
• **Economic factors:** Regions with better job opportunities, industries, and infrastructure attract more people, increasing population density.
 
• **Social factors:** Cultural and historical significance of certain areas might also contribute to higher population density.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Population Density:**
 
 
• Some **densely populated countries** include **India, Bangladesh, and Japan**. For instance, Delhi, India, has a very high population density due to urbanization.
 
• In contrast, countries like **Canada and Australia** have **low population density** due to large land areas and smaller populations.
 
• According to the **World Bank (2020)**, the global average population density is approximately **59 people per square kilometre**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Applications of Population Density:**

 
 
• **Urban planning:** Helps in designing cities, infrastructure, and public transport systems.
 
• **Environmental impact:** High population density can lead to increased pollution and resource depletion.
 
 
 
• **Global Comparisons:**
 
 
• **Monaco:** The country with the **highest population density**, approximately **26,150 people per square kilometre**.
 
• **Greenland:** One of the least densely populated areas with **0.03 people per square kilometre** due to its harsh climate.

questions.question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct option:

Assertion (A): Population explosion happens when the death rate drops but birth rate stays high.

Reason (R): Birth rate reduces immediately when health improves.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A is true, but R is false.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Population explosion** occurs when the **death rate decreases** while the **birth rate remains consistently high**. This is because the number of births outpaces the number of deaths, leading to rapid population growth. *Hence, the assertion (A) is correct.*
 
• The **birth rate** does not reduce immediately when health improves. While improvements in healthcare can lead to a decrease in the death rate (due to better medical facilities, sanitation, and nutrition), the birth rate often takes time to decline. This is due to factors such as cultural norms, lack of access to family planning, or socioeconomic conditions. *Hence, the reason (R) is false.*
 
• The **demographic transition model** illustrates this phenomenon: initially, improvements in healthcare reduce the death rate, but the birth rate remains high, leading to population explosion. Over time, with economic development and education, the birth rate begins to decline. This process can span decades, further supporting the idea that reason (R) is incorrect in explaining the assertion.
 
• In summary, the assertion (A) is true because population explosion occurs when the death rate drops but the birth rate remains high. However, the reason (R) is false because the birth rate does not reduce immediately due to improved health. Other factors like education, family planning, and cultural changes play a critical role over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Population Explosion:**

 
 
• **Definition:** A rapid increase in population due to higher birth rates and lower death rates. This often occurs during the early stages of development in a society.
 
• **Causes:** Improvements in healthcare, sanitation, and nutrition lead to a decline in mortality rates, while social and cultural factors may encourage high fertility rates.
 
• **Impact:** Population explosion can strain resources, lead to unemployment, environmental degradation, and challenges in providing healthcare and education.
 
 
 
• **Demographic Transition Model:**
 
 
• This model describes the transformation of countries from having high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates as they develop economically.
 
• It is divided into four stages:
 
 
• **Stage 1:** High birth and death rates, resulting in a stable population.
 
• **Stage 2:** Death rates decline due to health improvements, but birth rates remain high, causing population explosion.
 
• **Stage 3:** Birth rates begin to decline as economic and social changes occur.
 
• **Stage 4:** Both birth and death rates are low, leading to population stabilization.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Birth Rates:**
 
 
• **Socioeconomic Conditions:** Economic development and access to education, especially for women, are critical in reducing birth rates.
 
• **Healthcare Access:** Availability of reproductive healthcare and family planning methods significantly influence fertility rates.
 
• **Cultural Norms:** Societal expectations and religious beliefs may encourage large families, delaying the decline in birth rates.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Population Control Measures:**

 
 
• **Education:** Educating people about the benefits of family planning and smaller families can help control population growth.
 
• **Healthcare:** Improving access to contraception and reproductive healthcare services can reduce unintended pregnancies.
 
• **Government Policies:** Many countries have implemented population control policies, such as China's one-child policy (now relaxed to two or three children).

questions.question: The purpose of generative design in aerospace engineering is mainly to —
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Create lighter and stronger structures**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Generative design** is an advanced computational design process that uses algorithms to explore multiple design possibilities based on specific constraints and requirements.
 
• In aerospace engineering, the primary purpose of generative design is to **create lighter and stronger structures** to enhance aircraft performance and efficiency. *Hence, this option is correct.*
 
• Generative design helps optimize the use of materials, reducing the overall weight of aerospace components while maintaining structural integrity, which is critical for flight safety and fuel efficiency.
 
• By leveraging generative design, engineers can develop components like wings, fuselages, and propellers that are both lighter and capable of withstanding high stress during operation.
 
• This design approach incorporates factors such as **aerodynamic efficiency, load distribution, and material durability**, ensuring optimal performance in aerospace applications.
 
• Other options like improving pilot control systems, enhancing thrust generation, and developing new thermal shields are important in aerospace engineering but are not the primary purpose of generative design. These functions are achieved through other specialized technologies and engineering processes. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*
 
• Generative design in aerospace focuses on material optimization and structural efficiency, which aligns directly with the goal of creating lighter and stronger structures. *Hence, the correct answer is "Create lighter and stronger structures."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Generative Design in Aerospace Engineering:**

 
 
• Generative design is highly beneficial in aerospace due to its ability to **reduce weight and improve material efficiency**, which directly impacts fuel consumption and reduces operational costs.
 
• This computational process uses **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **machine learning algorithms** to explore thousands of design permutations in a short time.
 
• Examples of generative design applications in aerospace include the development of lightweight brackets, optimized engine components, and advanced aerodynamic surfaces.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Generative Design:**
 
 
• Generative design focuses on constraints such as weight, stress, and manufacturing techniques to provide optimal solutions.
 
• It integrates material science, engineering principles, and computational power to deliver designs that are structurally sound and efficient.
 
• **Example:** Generative design has been used by companies like **Airbus** and **Boeing** to create components that are 40%-60% lighter than traditional designs while maintaining strength and durability.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Aerospace Engineering:**
 
 
• Generative design is applied in creating **aircraft structural components**, engine parts, and space exploration vehicles.
 
• It also facilitates the use of advanced materials like **carbon composites**, **titanium alloys**, and **aluminum** to reduce weight and enhance strength.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages of Generative Design:**

 
 
• Generative design supports **additive manufacturing (3D printing)**, enabling the production of complex geometries that were previously impossible with traditional manufacturing methods.
 
• It reduces **material waste** and allows engineers to test various design iterations virtually, saving both time and resources.
 
 
 
• **Future Implications:**
 
 
• Generative design is expected to play a crucial role in **space exploration** by enabling the creation of efficient designs for spacecraft and Mars rovers.
 
• It aligns with the aerospace industry's goals of sustainability, efficiency, and technological advancement.

__
 
• **Statement 1:** Article 270 deals with **tax sharing** between the **Union** and the **States**. It outlines the manner in which certain taxes collected by the Union are distributed between the Union and the States. This statement is ***correct***.
 
• **Statement 2:** After the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act (2016)**, the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** was introduced. GST revenues collected by the Union are now shared with the states under Article 270, as part of the tax-sharing mechanism. This statement is ***correct***.
 
• **Statement 3:** **Compensation Cess** is not shared under Article 270. The Compensation Cess is specifically collected to compensate states for revenue losses due to the implementation of GST and is governed by the **GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017**. Therefore, it does not fall under Article 270. This statement is ***incorrect***.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 1 and 2 only.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 270 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• **Article 270** specifies the manner in which taxes are shared between the Union and the States.
 
• Taxes such as **Income Tax, Excise Duty, GST, and others** collected by the Union are distributed among the states according to the recommendations of the **Finance Commission**.
 
• The **101st Constitutional Amendment** added provisions for sharing GST revenues between the Union and the States under Article 270.
 
 
 
• **GST and Tax Sharing:**
 
 
• The **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** was introduced in **2017** to replace multiple indirect taxes. It is shared between the Union and States, ensuring equitable revenue distribution.
 
• Under the **GST regime**, states receive their share of taxes collected by the Union through Article 270.
 
 
 
• **Compensation Cess:**
 
 
• The **Compensation Cess** is collected under the **GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017** and is used to compensate states for potential revenue losses due to GST implementation.
 
• It is not included under Article 270 as it is meant solely for compensating states for losses, rather than tax-sharing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• The **Finance Commission** recommends the distribution of tax revenues between the Union and States under Article 270.
 
• It ensures fairness in revenue distribution based on criteria such as population, income distance, and area.
 
 
 
• **101st Constitutional Amendment:**
 
 
• Passed in **2016**, this amendment introduced the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**, a unified indirect tax regime replacing multiple taxes.
 
• It modified Article 270 to include provisions for sharing GST revenues between the Union and States.

questions.question: Farmers between which ages can join the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18–40 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY):** This scheme was launched by the **Government of India** to provide social security to small and marginal farmers by ensuring them financial stability after the age of 60 years.
 
• **Eligibility Age:** Farmers between the ages of **18 and 40 years** are eligible to enroll in the PM-KMY. *This statement is correct.*
 
• **Purpose:** The scheme aims to offer a regular pension of **INR 3,000 per month** to eligible farmers after they attain the age of 60 years.
 
• **Contribution:** Farmers need to contribute a monthly amount ranging from **INR 55 to INR 200**, depending on their entry age. The government makes an equal contribution to the farmer's pension fund.
 
• **Implementation:** The scheme is implemented by the **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare**. It is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme.
 
• **Incorrect Age Brackets:** The options like "18–30 years," "21–45 years," and "25–50 years" are incorrect, as the scheme explicitly defines the eligible age group as **18 to 40 years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objective of PM-KMY:**

 
 
• The scheme is aimed at providing **social security** to farmers who do not have any pension scheme after retirement.
 
• It seeks to safeguard the lives of small and marginal farmers in old age when they are no longer able to earn a livelihood.
 
• The scheme ensures **financial independence** and dignified living for farmers post-retirement.
 
 
 
• **Features of PM-KMY:**
 
 
• **Voluntary Scheme:** Farmers can voluntarily join the scheme by contributing a monthly premium.
 
• **Age-Based Contribution:** Farmers aged 18 years need to contribute INR 55 per month, while those aged 40 years need to contribute INR 200 per month.
 
• **Government Contribution:** The central government contributes an equal amount to the farmer's pension account.
 
• **Benefits:** After attaining 60 years of age, farmers receive a monthly pension of INR 3,000.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• The applicant must be a **small or marginal farmer** owning cultivable land up to **2 hectares.**
 
• Farmers must fall within the age bracket of **18 to 40 years** at the time of enrollment.
 
• The farmer must not be enrolled in any other government pension scheme.
 
 
 
• **Enrollment Process:**
 
 
• Farmers can enroll through the **Common Service Centers (CSCs)**.
 
• The enrollment requires **Aadhaar** and bank account details.
 
• After verification, the farmer can start contributing to the scheme.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Small and Marginal Farmers:** These are farmers who own cultivable land up to **2 hectares**. They are the primary beneficiaries of the PM-KMY scheme.
 
• **Exit from the Scheme:** In case of the death of the farmer before 60 years of age, the spouse can continue the scheme or withdraw the contributions with interest.
 
• **Key Facts:**
 
 
• The scheme was launched on **12 September 2019**.
 
• It is a part of the government’s effort to ensure **social security for unorganized sectors**, particularly farmers.
 
• Farmers who are beneficiaries of **PM-Kisan** are also eligible to join this scheme.

• **Assertion (A): The UDAN scheme was launched to promote regional air connectivity.**

 
 
• The **UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik)** scheme was launched in **2016** under the Ministry of Civil Aviation.
 
• The primary objective of the scheme is to make air travel affordable and accessible to the common citizens residing in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.
 
• It promotes regional air connectivity by linking under-served and unserved airports across the country.
 
• **Hence, the Assertion (A) is correct.**
 
 
 
• **Reason (R): Airlines are given Viability Gap Funding under the scheme.**
 
 
• The government provides **Viability Gap Funding (VGF)** to airlines under the UDAN scheme to ensure the economic feasibility of operations.
 
• VGF is provided to airlines to subsidize the cost of operations for routes that are otherwise unprofitable but essential for regional connectivity.
 
• This funding is shared between the central government and the state governments, with the central government typically providing 80% of the funding.
 
• The funding compensates for the capped airfares under the scheme to make tickets affordable for passengers.
 
• **Hence, the Reason (R) is correct, and it is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Objectives of the UDAN Scheme:**

 
 
• To make air travel affordable and widespread, catering to the needs of the common citizen.
 
• To enhance regional connectivity by developing infrastructure at under-served and unserved airports.
 
• To promote balanced regional economic growth and boost tourism and employment opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the UDAN Scheme:**
 
 
• Capped airfares: Ticket prices for one-hour flights on regional routes are capped at **INR 2,500** to make air travel affordable.
 
• Viability Gap Funding: Financial assistance is provided to airlines to offset losses incurred due to low ticket prices.
 
• Development of regional airports: Focus on developing and operationalizing **underutilized or unserved airports** across India.
 
• Public-Private Partnership (PPP): Encourages private sector participation in the aviation sector.
 
• Priority routes: Routes connecting remote, hilly, and northeastern areas are prioritized.
 
 
 
• **Achievements of the UDAN Scheme:**
 
 
• As of **2023**, more than **450 routes** have been operationalized, connecting several remote and smaller cities.
 
• Improved connectivity has boosted tourism and local economic development in several regions.
 
• The scheme has encouraged the establishment of new airlines catering to regional routes.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The UDAN scheme aligns with the government's mission of **‘Sab Uden, Sab Juden’** (Let everyone fly, let everyone connect).
 
• It has been implemented in multiple phases to accommodate growing demand and identify new routes.
 
• The scheme also supports helicopter and seaplane operations to further expand connectivity to remote areas.

questions.question: According to the Global Cities Index 2025 by Oxford Economics, which two cities topped the list?

• London and New York are viewed as benchmarks for urban development, offering insights into how cities can thrive in the **21st century**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is London and New York.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which statement about light industries is correct?

options.text: They use light materials to produce consumer goods.
They deal with power generation equipment.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They use light materials to produce consumer goods.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Light industries** are characterized by their use of **lightweight materials**, such as plastics, textiles, and chemicals, to produce **consumer goods**. These industries are focused on products intended for everyday use rather than heavy-duty applications.
 
• The primary goal of light industries is to create goods that cater to the needs of **individual consumers**, such as clothing, furniture, and electronics.
 
• Light industries typically require **less capital investment**, use **small-scale machinery**, and consume fewer resources compared to heavy industries. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• The statement “They manufacture heavy machinery” does not apply to light industries. Heavy machinery is produced by **heavy industries**, which require large-scale operations and infrastructure. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• The statement “They process ores and metals” is also incorrect. Processing of ores and metals is typically done by **mining and metallurgical industries**, which fall under the category of heavy industries. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• The statement “They deal with power generation equipment” refers to industries involved in manufacturing equipment for energy production, such as turbines and generators, which are part of **heavy engineering industries**. This does not align with the definition of light industries. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is “They use light materials to produce consumer goods.”***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Light Industries:**

 
 
• Light industries focus on producing **small-scale and lightweight goods**, such as clothing, food products, and consumer electronics.
 
• These industries typically operate in **urban areas**, where labor is easily accessible, and the demand for consumer goods is high.
 
• They contribute significantly to the **economic development** of a country by generating employment and producing goods for export.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Light Industries:**
 
 
• **Textile industry:** Produces clothing, fabrics, and apparel for personal use.
 
• **Electronics industry:** Includes consumer electronics such as smartphones, laptops, and household appliances.
 
• **Food processing industry:** Deals with packaged food, beverages, and dairy products.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Heavy Industries:**
 
 
• While light industries focus on **consumer goods**, heavy industries are involved in the production of **capital goods** such as machinery, steel, and equipment.
 
• Light industries require **less energy** and infrastructure than heavy industries, making them more sustainable in the long term.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Functions of Light Industries:**

 
 
• Light industries are essential for fulfilling the **basic needs** of consumers by supplying everyday products.
 
• They play a key role in **export-oriented economies**, where consumer goods are manufactured for international markets.
 
 
 
• **Global Examples of Light Industries:**
 
 
• **China:** Known for its large-scale production of consumer electronics and textiles, which dominate global markets.
 
• **India:** Home to thriving light industries like garment manufacturing and food processing, contributing significantly to its GDP.
 
• **United States:** Focuses on high-end consumer goods such as branded electronics and packaged foods.

questions.question: Schedule VII of the Indian Constitution contains —
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three legislative lists**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Schedule VII** of the **Indian Constitution** categorically deals with the division of powers between the **Union and the State Governments**.
 
• It contains the **Three legislative lists**, namely the **Union List**, the **State List**, and the **Concurrent List**. These lists specify the subjects on which respective governments can legislate.
 
• **Union List:** This list includes subjects on which only the **Parliament** can make laws. Examples include defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and banking.
 
• **State List:** This list includes subjects on which only the **State Legislatures** can make laws. Examples include police, public health, agriculture, and local government.
 
• **Concurrent List:** This list includes subjects on which both the **Parliament** and the **State Legislatures** can legislate. Examples include education, marriage, bankruptcy, and trade unions.
 
• The division of legislative powers ensures a federal structure by defining the areas of governance for both levels of government.
 
• *Hence, Schedule VII of the Indian Constitution contains the Three legislative lists.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Union List:**

 
 
• The **Union List** currently has **97 subjects**. The Union Government has exclusive power to legislate on these subjects.
 
• Some important subjects in the Union List include **defense**, **foreign affairs**, **currency**, **railways**, and **citizenship**.
 
 
 
• **State List:**
 
 
• The **State List** includes **61 subjects**. The State Legislatures have exclusive power to legislate on these subjects unless the Constitution provides otherwise.
 
• Subjects like **land**, **agriculture**, **police**, and **local government** are included in the State List.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List:**
 
 
• The **Concurrent List** consists of **52 subjects**. Both the Union and State Governments can legislate on these subjects.
 
• In case of conflict, the law enacted by the **Union Government** prevails over the State law.
 
• Subjects like **education**, **trade unions**, and **criminal law** fall under the Concurrent List.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Schedule VII:**
 
 
• Schedule VII is crucial for maintaining the **federal structure** of India by clearly defining the legislative areas of the Union and State Governments.
 
• It reduces the chances of overlapping legislation and ensures administrative efficiency.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Background:**

 
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1935** served as the foundation for the legislative division in Schedule VII.
 
• The act introduced the concept of federalism by categorizing subjects into lists, which was later adopted in the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• **Amendments:**
 
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act, 1976** added subjects like education and forests to the Concurrent List.
 
• Certain subjects have been moved between lists based on socio-economic and political requirements.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Interpretation:**
 
 
• The judiciary has played a crucial role in resolving conflicts arising due to overlapping subjects between the Union and State Lists.
 
• The principle of federal supremacy ensures that Union laws prevail in case of conflict.

questions.question: Constructing sea walls and raising houses to tackle rising sea levels is an example of —
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Climate change adaptation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Climate change adaptation** refers to actions and strategies aimed at adjusting or modifying systems, structures, or behaviors to minimize the negative impacts of climate change.
 
• Constructing sea walls and raising houses to tackle rising sea levels are direct examples of adaptation, as they help communities adjust to current and anticipated changes in environmental conditions caused by climate change.
 
• Adaptation measures focus on reducing vulnerability to climate-related hazards such as floods, droughts, and rising sea levels. These measures are often location-specific and address the immediate needs of affected communities. *Hence, the given example is correct.*
 
• Unlike mitigation, adaptation does not aim to prevent climate change but rather seeks to manage its consequences effectively. For instance, constructing infrastructure like levees, flood barriers, and elevated buildings is a common adaptation strategy.
 
• Adaptation strategies are often implemented by governments, communities, and organizations in response to specific environmental challenges such as coastal erosion, water scarcity, or extreme weather events. *Hence, adaptation is the most suitable term for this example.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Climate change mitigation:**

 
 
• Mitigation refers to efforts to reduce or prevent the emission of greenhouse gases, aiming to slow down or reverse climate change.
 
• Examples include transitioning to renewable energy sources like **solar and wind energy**, improving energy efficiency, and reforestation to absorb **carbon dioxide**.
 
• Mitigation focuses on reducing the causes of climate change rather than managing its effects. For example, reducing fossil fuel usage is a mitigation effort.
 
 
 
• **Carbon sequestration:**
 
 
• Carbon sequestration involves capturing and storing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to reduce greenhouse gas concentrations.
 
• **Examples:** Planting trees, which absorb CO₂, and using carbon capture and storage (CCS) technology in industrial processes.
 
• It is primarily used as a mitigation strategy rather than adaptation, as it focuses on addressing the root causes of climate change.
 
 
 
• **Geoengineering:**
 
 
• Geoengineering includes large-scale interventions in the Earth’s climate system to counteract climate change.
 
• Examples include injecting aerosols into the atmosphere to reflect sunlight or artificial carbon capture methods.
 
• Geoengineering is experimental and controversial due to its potential unintended consequences on ecosystems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Adaptation Strategies:**

 
 
• Adaptation strategies are critical for communities already experiencing the impacts of climate change. Examples include constructing flood-resistant buildings and improving water management systems in drought-prone areas.
 
• Developing early warning systems for extreme weather events is another effective adaptation measure.
 
 
 
• **Global Efforts:**
 
 
• The **Paris Agreement** emphasizes the importance of adaptation alongside mitigation to address climate change comprehensively.
 
• The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (**UNFCCC**) encourages countries to develop national adaptation plans to safeguard vulnerable populations.

questions.question: The quantity that keeps a satellite in its orbit without continuous propulsion is —
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Orbital velocity**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Satellites are kept in orbit due to the balance between their **gravitational pull** and their forward motion.
 
• **Gravitational pull**, which is the force exerted by the Earth, pulls the satellite toward the planet, preventing it from flying off into space.
 
• At the same time, the satellite's forward motion, or **orbital velocity**, prevents it from falling directly back to Earth, allowing it to move in a curved path around the planet.
 
• This balance between gravitational pull and orbital velocity creates a stable orbit, ensuring that the satellite maintains its path without requiring continuous propulsion. *Hence, the correct answer is "Orbital velocity."*
 
• Other factors, such as mass, atmospheric pressure, and propulsion, play a role in a satellite's design, but they are not the primary forces that keep it in orbit.

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gravitational Pull:**

 
 
• The gravitational force is a universal force that attracts two objects with mass toward each other. It is given by the formula F = G*(m1*m2)/r², where **G** is the gravitational constant, **m1** and **m2** are the masses of the two objects, and **r** is the distance between their centers.
 
• For satellites, the gravitational pull of the Earth provides the centripetal force needed to keep them in a circular or elliptical orbit.
 
 
 
• **Orbital Velocity:**
 
 
• Orbital velocity is the minimum speed required for a satellite to maintain a stable orbit. It depends on the mass of the planet and the distance of the satellite from the planet's center.
 
• For Earth, the average orbital velocity near its surface is approximately **7.9 km/s**.
 
• If a satellite's speed exceeds the escape velocity, it will leave Earth's gravitational pull and move into space.
 
 
 
• **Other Factors:**
 
 
• **Mass:** While the mass of a satellite affects its inertia, it does not influence the gravitational pull experienced by the satellite, as acceleration due to gravity is independent of mass.
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure:** Atmospheric pressure affects objects within the Earth's atmosphere but is negligible for satellites in orbit because they are in near-vacuum conditions.
 
• **Propulsion:** Satellites do not require continuous propulsion to remain in orbit. Propulsion is typically used for minor adjustments or to change orbits.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Geostationary Satellites:**

 
 
• Geostationary satellites orbit at an altitude of approximately **35,786 km** above the equator. They appear stationary relative to the Earth's surface and are used for communication and weather monitoring.
 
 
 
• **Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Satellites:**
 
 
• LEO satellites orbit at altitudes between **160 km to 2,000 km** and are used for applications like Earth observation, remote sensing, and some communication networks.
 
 
 
• **Escape Velocity:**
 
 
• Escape velocity is the minimum speed needed for an object to break free from a planet's gravitational pull. For Earth, it is approximately **11.2 km/s**.
